People still ask about the name from time to time, especially in the middle of a Hội An summer.

The Hill Station actually began in the winter of 2011, up in the cold mist of Sa Pa, built around a warm fire, simple comfort food, and a room full of travelers and expats who stayed a little longer than planned.

When we looked for a second home in 2015, we had our eyes on Hà Nội and Luang Prabang. Then we stumbled across a weathered old house in Hội An. Within days we were on a flight; by October, the doors were open.

Eleven years on, the façade hasn’t changed all that much and neither has the idea behind it.

Hà Nội’s heat can be hard on people, but it does something remarkable to whisky. The city’s swing between sticky summers and cold winters is why Về Để Đi built Vietnam’s first independent whisky distillery there.

Their corn whisky begins with an heirloom variety grown in the northern highlands and is aged through those changing seasons. The result is honeyed and creamy, with notes of palm sugar and toasted oak.

It forms the base of Về Để Đi’s Old Fashioned. At The Hill Station, the finished cocktail is poured over one large cube of ice and garnished with dried orange. Nothing more needed.
